Subject: Robert asked about AI stocks after earnings
Body: Robert Hartwell called after the latest round of earnings headlines and asked whether the trust should buy Nvidia shares directly. Reminded him the trust already owns Nvidia through APKAX and the Global Technology Fund, so a direct position would stack single-stock risk on top of the fund exposure, which the trustees have asked the firm to avoid. Mentioned that the research team (Meredith Calloway, Arjun Mehta) published its GPU demand outlook yesterday; offered to send a copy. Robert agreed to hold off. No action.

Subject: Elaine concerned about technology concentration
Body: Elaine Hartwell called, concerned that technology has become too large a share of the trust and that Nvidia shows up in more than one fund, notably the Global Technology Fund and the AI Infrastructure Fund. Confirmed there is overlap between the two funds' largest holdings. Told her the Investment Committee may revisit the AI allocation at its February meeting; nothing has been decided. Elaine wants figures, not reassurance. Will review at the Q1 meeting with both trustees.

Subject: Quarterly review - AI allocation and look-through request
Body: Quarterly review with Robert Hartwell and Elaine Hartwell for the Hartwell Family Trust. Reviewed the IC-2026-004 purchases of the AI Infrastructure Fund: $957,484 in the trust taxable account (February 17) and $184,492 in Robert's rollover IRA (February 20). Robert supportive of the AI view. Elaine asked for the family's total Nvidia exposure across the AI Infrastructure Fund and the Global Technology Fund; look-through request sent to the risk team today. Told the trustees Private Credit Fund II may call capital in the spring; amount and timing not yet known.

Subject: Capital call questions - Private Credit Fund II
Body: Robert Hartwell called with questions on Private Credit Fund II capital call #6 ($700,000 due April 20). Explained that the call finances a new senior secured term loan to Cobalt Ridge Data Centers, a data center developer building a campus in West Texas, approved by the Investment Committee on April 9 (IC-2026-006). Loan is first lien on the land, buildings and power equipment, with maintenance covenants. Robert asked whether this adds to the trust's technology exposure; explained it is a loan rather than equity, though it does add some data center exposure that the risk team's look-through work will capture. Robert comfortable; wire to go from the private investments account per instructions on file.

Subject: Elaine comfortable with overlap reduction
Body: Elaine Hartwell called and approved the August 3 overlap trades under IC-2026-011: Global Technology Fund sales of about $3.17 million in the trust account and about $608,000 in Robert Hartwell's rollover IRA, per the plan emailed July 20. She then asked about power risk at Cobalt Ridge Data Centers, specifically what happens to the Private Credit Fund II loan if the campus's grid interconnection is delayed. Agreed to cover it at the August 12 mid-year review with Brendan Kessler; will get a briefing from Marcus Bell's team beforehand. Approval passed to the trading desk.

Subject: Robert asked about Nvidia volatility
Body: Robert Hartwell called about the recent swings in Nvidia and asked whether the firm's view has changed. Shared Meredith Calloway's Q3 review: GPU capacity remains tight and the team expects demand to hold through 2027. The Investment Committee kept the AI Infrastructure Fund at 8% of Growth models on September 10 (IC-2026-013), and the fund holds Nvidia at its 10% single-name cap. Also confirmed capital call #7 ($350,000) was funded on September 15; it financed Private Credit Fund II's new senior secured facility to Polar Loop Cooling Systems, a liquid cooling manufacturer. Robert comfortable; no changes.

Subject: Private credit interest
Body: Chinedu Okafor called to ask whether the family office could add to private credit. Explained that the Okafor Family Office's commitment to Private Credit Fund II is set; additional exposure comes only as the undrawn balance is called for new loans. Discussed direct lending yields versus core bonds and the floating-rate structure of the fund's loans: coupons reset with short-term rates, so income would drift lower if policy rates are cut, but there is little duration risk. Chinedu Okafor accepted the explanation and asked to hear about new loans as they reach the Investment Committee. No change to the commitment.

Subject: Portfolio review - AI allocation
Body: Portfolio review with Chinedu Okafor and Ngozi Okafor for the Okafor Family Office. Walked through IC-2026-004 and the purchase of about $1.20 million of the AI Infrastructure Fund scheduled for February 25 in the taxable account, funded from the Municipal Income Fund. Chinedu supportive and asked about going above the model weight; recommended staying at model given the existing technology overweight. Ngozi Okafor asked about liquidity; confirmed the fund trades daily and the purchase does not touch cash set aside for Private Credit Fund II, where she wants commitments kept steady and early notice of any capital call. Both want the client-directed technology overweight kept, provided it is documented. To do: send an updated IPS acknowledging the overweight for signature; confirm the trade after settlement.

Subject: Overlap reduction
Body: Called Chinedu Okafor to walk through the IC-2026-011 overlap-reduction trades scheduled for July 29 in the Okafor Family Office taxable account: sell about $4.27 million of the Global Technology Fund and reinvest the proceeds in the Cybersecurity Leaders Fund and the Core Fixed Income Fund. Explained that the June 15 look-through put the family office at 16.3%, above the firm's 15% guideline, mainly because Nvidia is held in both the Global Technology Fund and the AI Infrastructure Fund; the trades target about 13%. Chinedu Okafor was reluctant - the technology overweight was his choice and he still believes in it - but agreed once it was clear this is risk management, not a change in the firm's view on GPU demand. Consent documented. Will send an estimate of the realized gain before the trade date.

Subject: IPS fossil-fuel exclusion reminder
Body: Margaret Bellamy called to remind us that the Bellamy Foundation's investment policy excludes fossil-fuel infrastructure, including midstream pipelines; her board asked her to reconfirm after recent press coverage of gas-fired power for data centers. Confirmed the foundation holds no Energy Infrastructure Fund and was left out of the IC-2025-014 initiation in June 2025 for that reason. Its energy allocation is the Clean Energy Transition Fund. Checked that the exclusion is still coded as a restriction on the endowment pool account, so model trades into the Energy Infrastructure Fund cannot be placed there. Margaret satisfied; no action.

Subject: Investment review
Body: Investment review with Margaret Bellamy. Confirmed the Bellamy Foundation is exempt from IC-2026-008 because its investment policy excludes fossil-fuel infrastructure; the account will be left out of the June Energy Infrastructure Fund rebalancing. Its energy allocation stays in the Clean Energy Transition Fund, and she said the board is comfortable with that weight. She asked whether the foundation is indirectly exposed to data center power demand; explained that the AI Infrastructure Fund, held through the Balanced model, owns Constellation Energy and Quanta Services, which are power generation and grid construction companies rather than fossil-fuel pipelines, and that both also appear in the Clean Energy Transition Fund. She wants figures for the board, not a description: look-through report requested. Written recap of the exemption to follow.

Subject: Tax-loss harvesting review
Body: Erik Lindqvist called to ask whether there are losses worth harvesting in the trust before year-end. Reviewed the taxable trust account: the Healthcare Innovation Fund is close to its cost basis, so a sale would realize little loss and take the trust out of the position. Erik asked about the weakness in Novo Nordisk; explained it is one of the fund's holdings alongside Eli Lilly and that Hannah Schultz's team sees it as a question of competitive position in GLP-1 therapies, not a reason to exit the theme. The IRA is not a candidate because losses there carry no tax benefit. Agreed no harvest this year; will revisit next December.

Subject: Rebalance confirmation
Body: Called Erik Lindqvist to confirm the Balanced-model purchases of the AI Infrastructure Fund under IC-2026-004, which raised the fund's weight in the Balanced model from 3% to 5%: $194,517 in the Lindqvist Revocable Trust account on March 5, funded from the Municipal Income Fund, and $41,062 in his IRA on February 18, funded from the Core Fixed Income Fund. Erik asked why the two accounts traded about two weeks apart; explained the desk spread the rebalance over February 17 to March 6, roughly four accounts a day. Erik fine with the size of the change and comfortable with the firm's view that demand for GPU capacity holds through 2027; no follow-up needed.

Subject: Planning meeting
Body: Planning meeting with Carlos Ramirez and Sofia Ramirez. College funding: their daughter starts in about three years; compared earmarking part of the joint taxable account with opening a 529 plan, and will model both. The Municipal Income Fund position in the joint account continues to provide federally tax-exempt income; with no state income tax in Texas, that is the main benefit. Sofia asked what rate cuts would mean for their municipal bonds; explained that bonds already held generally gain value as rates fall while reinvested income earns less, and that our fixed income team expects cuts to come more gradually than the market hopes. Sofia also asked about GLP-1 headlines; noted the Healthcare Innovation Fund already holds Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk. No changes; next meeting in the spring.

Subject: Energy allocation change
Body: Called Carlos Ramirez about the Energy Infrastructure Fund purchase scheduled for June 12 in the joint taxable account: $97,219, funded from the Municipal Income Fund, implementing IC-2026-008, which raises the fund from 5% to 7% of the Balanced model. Explained the committee's thesis: power demand from AI data centers is growing faster than the grid can add capacity, much of the new supply is expected to come from gas-fired generation, and the fund's pipeline operators should move more volume under largely fee-based contracts. Carlos Ramirez asked whether this is a bet on natural gas prices; explained the fund's pipeline holdings earn mostly fee-based revenue tied to volumes rather than commodity prices. Carlos fine with it; no restrictions on the joint account.

Subject: Annual grant distribution
Body: Diane Whitman called to confirm the Whitman Charitable Foundation's annual grant distribution of $600,000. Agreed to raise the cash by selling $600,000 of the Core Fixed Income Fund on February 3; bonds are the largest part of the foundation's conservative allocation, so funding from there leaves the equity funds untouched and has little effect on the overall mix. Proceeds to be wired to the foundation's operating account on settlement under the standing instructions on file; Courtney Bianchi to confirm by phone with Diane Whitman before release. Diane asked for written confirmation for the grants committee once funds arrive.

Subject: Duration question
Body: Diane Whitman emailed asking why the foundation's bond allocation has been steadier this year than in prior years. Replied the same day. In March the Investment Committee approved IC-2026-005, which shortened the Core Fixed Income Fund duration target from 6.0 to 5.0 years. A shorter duration target makes the fund less sensitive to moves in long-term yields, which has helped dampen swings in the foundation's bond holdings; the trade-off is less upside if yields fall sharply. The change was made inside the fund, mainly by selling longer-dated Treasuries, and required no trades in the foundation's account. Diane plans to share the explanation with her board; offered a call with the board if useful.

Subject: Capital call - Private Credit Fund II
Body: Kenji Nakamura confirmed capital call #6 ($300,000) was funded on April 20 from the partnership's private investments account. He asked what the call is financing and how Private Credit Fund II is protected. Explained the structure: a $45 million senior secured term loan to Cobalt Ridge Data Centers, approved by the Investment Committee on April 9 (IC-2026-006), to build phase 1 of a 120 MW data center campus in West Texas. The loan is first lien on the land, buildings and power equipment, floats over SOFR, and carries maintenance covenants and a debt service reserve. Phase 1 has tenant commitments from an investment-grade hyperscale tenant and a GPU cloud operator, and power is contracted under a long-term power purchase agreement. Kenji satisfied; closing expected shortly.

Subject: Polar Loop facility
Body: Kenji Nakamura confirmed capital call #7 ($150,000) was funded on September 15. It finances Private Credit Fund II's new $20 million senior secured facility to Polar Loop Cooling Systems (IC-2026-013, approved September 10), which pays for a second manufacturing line. Kenji asked whether demand for liquid cooling is durable or a one-cycle spike. Shared the firm's view: rack density in new GPU deployments has moved past what air cooling can handle, so direct-to-chip liquid cooling is becoming the standard design for new AI data centers, and Polar Loop's order backlog has grown with it. Also noted that Polar Loop supplies the cooling for the Cobalt Ridge Data Centers campus, so the private credit team monitors the two loans as related exposure. Kenji comfortable; no action.

Subject: RMD and income needs
Body: Called Maria Delgado to confirm her required minimum distribution for the year: $74,450.07 was paid from her IRA on December 10, raised by selling Core Fixed Income Fund shares, and Maria confirmed receipt. Reviewed her income needs for next year. Distributions from the Municipal Income Fund in the Delgado Family Trust are adequate to cover her regular expenses, so no change to the trust allocation is needed. Maria wants the trust to stay income-focused. Will schedule next year's RMD for the fourth quarter as usual.

Subject: Rate cuts question
Body: Maria Delgado called to ask how rate cuts would affect the income she draws from her accounts. Explained that the Core Fixed Income Fund's yield would drift lower gradually as maturing bonds are reinvested, rather than drop all at once, and that the firm expects fewer rate cuts than the market is pricing. Also walked her through the shorter duration target adopted in March, from 6.0 to 5.0 years: the fund is now less sensitive to swings in long-term yields, at the cost of some price upside if yields fall sharply. The change was made inside the fund and required no trades in her IRA or the trust. Maria satisfied; no changes.

Subject: Endowment spending policy review
Body: Met with Helen Marsh to review the St. Aldric School Endowment's 5% spending policy ahead of the school's next budget cycle. No change proposed; Helen confirmed the board remains comfortable with the 5% rate and with funding the draws from fixed income. Also confirmed the Balanced-model purchase of the AI Infrastructure Fund under IC-2026-004: $299,108 on February 19, funded from the Core Fixed Income Fund, as the Balanced weight moved from 3% to 5%. Helen asked whether the larger position adds concentration risk; explained that the risk team is reviewing look-through exposure across funds, with results expected by mid-year. Helen comfortable; no further action.

Subject: AI rebalance confirmation
Body: Called Patrick Brennan to confirm the purchases of the AI Infrastructure Fund under IC-2026-004, which raised the Growth model weight from 5% to 8%. Joint account: $223,820 bought on February 24, funded from the Municipal Income Fund. IRA: $71,492 bought today, February 27, funded from the Core Fixed Income Fund. Patrick supportive of the committee's view that demand for GPU capacity holds through 2027. He asked about the tax effect of the Municipal Income Fund sale in the joint account; will confirm the realized gain or loss and send it to his CPA. No other changes.

Subject: Energy infrastructure question
Body: Patrick Brennan called about the $151,201 Energy Infrastructure Fund purchase in the joint account on June 11. Explained IC-2026-008: on May 14 the Investment Committee raised the fund from 5% to 7% of the Growth model, funded from the Municipal Income Fund in taxable accounts. The thesis is data center power demand: the firm expects much of the new power demand from AI data centers to be met by gas-fired generation, which means more volume through natural gas pipelines, mostly under fee-based contracts. Patrick asked whether this is a bet on gas prices; told him it is mainly a volume story with limited commodity exposure. He is comfortable; no further action.

Subject: Overlap reduction
Body: Walked Caroline Sterling-Hayes through the IC-2026-011 trades scheduled for August 5: sell about $3.32 million of the Global Technology Fund in the family office's taxable account and reinvest the proceeds in the Cybersecurity Leaders Fund and the Core Fixed Income Fund. June look-through AI exposure was 16.5%, above the 15% guideline, driven largely by Nvidia overlap between the Global Technology Fund and the AI Infrastructure Fund; the trades are sized to bring it to about 13%. Separately, the new 10% single-name cap trims Nvidia from 12% to 10% inside the AI Infrastructure Fund, with no trades needed in her accounts. Caroline agreed and acknowledged the technology overweight was set at her direction; consent documented.

Subject: Capital call confirmation
Body: Confirmed with Caroline Sterling-Hayes that capital call #6 ($800,000) was funded on April 20 from the family office's private investments account. Explained the use of proceeds: Private Credit Fund II is lending $45 million to Cobalt Ridge Data Centers under IC-2026-006, approved April 9, through a senior secured term loan financing phase 1 of a 120 MW campus in West Texas. Caroline asked what protects the fund if construction runs late. Covered the first lien on land, buildings and power equipment, the debt service reserve and the loan-to-value limit, along with Pemberton Grid Consulting's independent power assessment supporting the energization timeline. She is comfortable; closing targeted this week.

Subject: Conservative income review
Body: Income review call with Irina Volkov. Municipal Income Fund distributions in her individual account continue to cover her monthly spending. Irina asked whether current Treasury yields make it worth moving out of munis; compared the two on an after-tax basis, and for her bracket the tax-exempt income still compares well. Shared the fixed income team's view from the December Investment Committee meeting that rate cuts are likely to come more slowly than the market expects. Municipal bonds stay in the taxable account; the Roth's bond sleeve is the Core Fixed Income Fund, since tax-exempt income would add nothing there. No changes.
